title: Museo: colección de preparaciones microscópicas del siglo XIX
citation: IES San Isidro Madrid, Museo / Gabinete de Historia Natural, current collection record (2026).
tags: Spain; Madrid; secondary education; nineteenth century; teaching slides; Cajal inscription; natural history cabinet
note: The historic Natural History cabinet explicitly retains a collection of nineteenth-century microscopic preparations. The museum also notes older preparations displayed with an early-twentieth-century microscope, some carrying a Cajal inscription. No slide total is published, so broader teaching-museum counts are not repurposed as a preparation total.

title: Colección de Artrópodos no Insectos: preparaciones microscópicas
citation: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, “Artrópodos,” current collection record (2026).
tags: Spain; Madrid; arthropods; microscope slides; mites; Bathynellacea; decapods; nineteenth century; cabinets
note: The current MNCN arthropod collection reports more than 12,000 microscopic preparations stored in dedicated cabinets, including 2,832 mite and 2,731 Bathynellacea preparations. The same history records more than 10,000 recently located decapod preparations belonging partly to the late nineteenth century and partly to current collections; this subset is not added to the current total because its relationship to the 12,000-plus state is not stated as disjoint.

title: Preparacions microscòpiques
citation: Centre de Documentació de Biodiversitat Vegetal de la Universitat de Barcelona, “Preparacions microscòpiques,” current collection record (2026).
tags: Spain; Barcelona; herbarium; microscopic preparations; pollen; freshwater algae; Suárez Cervera; Hernández Mariné; Pando
note: A dedicated Catalan-language collection page for microscopic preparations. CeDocBiV separately identifies more than 500 preparations by M. Asunción Suárez Cervera, about 600 freshwater-microalgae preparations mainly by Mariona Hernández Mariné, a pollen-preparation collection, and 24 preparations made by Francisco Pando from Taurino Mariano Losa España herbarium material. The groups remain separate rather than being merged into one inferred total.

title: Microscopia vegetal
tags: Portugal; Brotéria; plant microscopy; permanent preparations; teaching; experimental natural history; Zimmermann
note: A four-part Portuguese technical series aimed at experimental natural-history teaching. Historical reconstruction states that the articles give detailed descriptions of instruments and methods for obtaining permanent preparations for microscopic observation. The row records the serial preparation-method sequence rather than a general microscopy manual.

title: Diatomaceas. Como se colhem e preparam
citation: Carlos Zimmermann, “Diatomaceas. Como se colhem e preparam,” Brotéria: Vulgarização Científica 9 (1910): 42–51.
tags: Portugal; diatoms; collecting; permanent mounting; slides; Brotéria; Zimmermann
note: A direct Portuguese-language account of collecting and preparing diatoms. Zimmermann's preparation literature is explicitly described as teaching readers how to collect diatoms and make permanent preparations for microscopic observation, making the physical preparation sequence the subject rather than an incidental step.

title: Jesuítas e Ciência em Portugal. II – Carlos Zimmermann S.J. e o ensino da Microscopia Vegetal
citation: Francisco Malta Romeiras and Henrique Leitão, “Jesuítas e Ciência em Portugal. II – Carlos Zimmermann S.J. e o ensino da Microscopia Vegetal,” Brotéria 174 (2012): 113–125.
tags: Portugal; Zimmermann; microscopy teaching; permanent preparations; Jesuits; São Fiel; technical pedagogy
note: A historical study of Zimmermann's experimental microscopy teaching and plant-microscopy programme, including the preparation protocols through which permanent microscopic objects entered classroom practice. It provides the research bridge for the 1902–06 and 1910 technical texts admitted in the same pass.

title: Los catálogos de material científico de microscopía como fuente para el análisis de las prácticas de la enseñanza de la biología moderna en España en la primera mitad del siglo XX
citation: José Pedro Marín Murcia, “Los catálogos de material científico de microscopía como fuente para el análisis de las prácticas de la enseñanza de la biología moderna en España en la primera mitad del siglo XX,” in Maria Cristina Morandini and Francesca Pizzigoni (eds.), Objects that Travel in Time: The Commercial Circulation of Educational Objects between the 19th and 20th Centuries (Lecce: Pensa MultiMedia, 2024), 111–137.
tags: Spain; teaching slides; commercial catalogues; Sigmund; Hensoldt; Leitz; Reichert; Madrid; Murcia; material culture
note: A microscopy-material study connecting commercial catalogues to surviving teaching collections in Spanish universities. It documents more than 800 Fernández Galiano preparations, a recently catalogued Sigmund collection of 25 cases with an initial inventory of 249 slides, and roughly one thousand Hensoldt preparations in the former University of Murcia biology laboratory, while distinguishing instruments, projection systems and prepared-slide collections.
